Taiwan Semiconductor, the world's largest chip foundry, is considering expanding its business into advanced storage chip manufacturing and has, at the request of its largest customer NVIDIA, begun formulating plans to produce 3D DRAM (three-dimensional dynamic random-access memory). The Zhitong Finance APP has learned that, according to media reports, Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM.US), the world's largest chip foundry, is considering expanding its business into advanced storage chip manufacturing and has, at the request of its largest customer NVIDIA (NVDA.US), begun formulating plans to produce 3D DRAM (three-dimensional dynamic random-access memory). If this plan is ultimately implemented, Taiwan Semiconductor could further expand its influence in the artificial intelligence (AI) hardware supply chain. According to media reports citing two insiders, Taiwan Semiconductor has recently begun studying production plans for 3D DRAM. This move stems from NVIDIA's demand for advanced memory chips and reflects that AI chip designers are actively seeking to diversify their sources of critical components. 3D DRAM is an advanced memory chip technology that employs a three-dimensional architecture, aiming to increase storage density through novel cell layouts and manufacturing processes, while providing more technological options for future high-performance computing systems. For Taiwan Semiconductor, which has long focused on logic chip foundry and advanced packaging, entering advanced DRAM manufacturing would mean further expanding its business portfolio. Currently, Taiwan Semiconductor dominates the global advanced logic chip manufacturing sector and is also a key manufacturing partner for NVIDIA's AI accelerators. If it further enters the advanced memory chip production field in the future, Taiwan Semiconductor will have the opportunity to play a role in more critical segments of AI computing hardware. This potential business expansion comes at a time when the global memory chip market is facing severe supply constraints. As the boom in generative AI and data center construction continues, demand for high-performance computing hardware and associated memory chips is surging, tightening supply and driving prices sharply higher. For AI chip designers such as NVIDIA, memory chips are a critical component that determines the performance and production scale of computing systems. Supply shortages could not only drive up hardware manufacturing costs but also constrain the pace of AI infrastructure deployment. Consequently, major tech companies, including NVIDIA and Apple (AAPL.US), are actively seeking additional sources of memory chip supply to mitigate supply chain risks. The impact of rising storage chip prices has also begun to ripple through the consumer electronics market. Earlier this year, Apple raised the prices of some products, citing higher storage costs, highlighting that the tight supply of storage chips is no longer confined to the AI server sector but is affecting a broader range of electronic product markets. Against this backdrop, NVIDIA is urging Taiwan Semiconductor to research 3D DRAM production, which may help it establish a more diversified advanced storage chip supply system in the future. However, the relevant plans are currently still in the preliminary research and planning stages. The report did not disclose the scale of funding Taiwan Semiconductor plans to invest, its potential production capacity, the mass-production timeline, or whether it will formally launch commercial production in the future. Furthermore, 3D DRAM is not entirely the same technological route as High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), which is widely used in current AI accelerators, and Taiwan Semiconductor's research into 3D DRAM production does not mean it has decided to enter the existing HBM market. Revenue in July rose 45% to NT$467.58 billion ($14.5 billion). Analysts on average are estimating a 46.8% increase in sales for the current quarter, Q3. The latest performance shows steady demand for advanced chips, which power data centers and other systems that power AI applications, smartphones and automobiles. TSMC makes cutting-edge semiconductors for the likes of Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices. The biggest buyers of those chips – including cloud companies Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft – have set aside about $800 billion for AI-related investments this year. Last month, TSMC raised its spending and revenue projections for the year, reflecting confidence in demand for chips powering AI development. TSMC now expects its capital expenditure to reach a record level of $60 billion to $64 billion in 2026 and forecasts its full-year sales to grow slightly above 40% in U.S. dollar terms. Separately, Sony Group and TSMC announced a plan to spend around ‌1 trillion yen ($6.32 billion) to jointly ‌make next-generation microchips used in image sensors, the Nikkei ​business daily said on Monday. A joint venture owned about 60% by Sony and 40% by TSMC will start commercial production as early ‌as 2029 in ⁠southern Japan's Kumamoto prefecture, the paper said. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for TSMC remained ‘bearish,’ unchanged from the previous day, with several users posting about the monthly update. TSM stock gained nearly 4% last week and is up 39% year to date. In comparison, the semiconductor benchmark iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) has increased nearly 80% over the past year. Shares of Rocket Lab (RKLB) and AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) rose 2.4% and 0.6%, respectively, in premarket trading Monday ahead of their quarterly results due after the market close, with both stocks showing signs of a strong setup. RKLB stock rose a sharp 27.5% this week while ASTS rose 22% boosted by SpaceX’s report in the week prior and new contract wins. SpaceX's revenue nearly doubled, the rocket company ​said in its first earnings report since going public, fueled by its booming Starlink satellite communications and AI businesses. The company reported April-June revenue of $7.8 billion, compared with $4.1 billion a year earlier, beating Wall Street expectations from analysts polled by ​LSEG/Reuters. Starlink revenue, which accounted for over half of total revenue, rose 66%, and revenue from SpaceX's AI business — which Musk has pitched as the company's future growth driver — surged about 250%. Revenue from the space segment, which includes commercial launches, government missions and development of Starship, revenue grew 29%. The results allayed investor concerns over SpaceX’s high spending, with the stock rising 16% since the quarterly report was issued on Aug. 3. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was ‘bullish’ for both RKLB and ASTS, with the tickers trending at various points earlier in the day. “$ASTS a beat and raise [is] imminent. AST SpaceMobile entered this quarter with roughly $1.2 billion in contracted revenue commitments. Then came J-LEO,” a trader said. “Japan approved up to 148B yen (~$900M+) of government support, covering up to 50% of eligible project costs. That implies roughly $1.8B+ of total project spending. Assume ~70% ultimately flows to AST for satellites, gateways and network infrastructure, with ~30% going toward Mitsubishi launch costs.” they said. On the RKLB stream, a trader wrote: “I’ve watched $RKLB for a long time and started building a position in early 2025. The more I dug in, the more it came back to Peter Beck. No theatrics, no constant hype — just engineering, execution and a long-term obsession with the mission. I’ve backed great founders before, and Beck gives me that same feeling. That’s why RKLB became a core holding for me.” Analysts expect Rocket Lab’s quarterly revenue to grow 15% from a quarter ago to $230.94 million, although its adjusted loss is projected to widen to $0.05 per share from $0.02, per estimates from Koyfin. Analysts expect AST SpaceMobile’s quarterly revenue to surge 133% from the previous quarter to $34.4 million, while its adjusted loss is projected to narrow to $0.23 per share from $0.66. Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO) CEO Strauss Zelnick said on Friday that the company was counting on the blockbuster launch of ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ to drive its next phase of growth after the video game maker reported quarterly results that topped Wall Street estimates. “Our excellent first quarter results reflect the power of our portfolio and disciplined execution across all of our labels,” Zelnick said. “With these positive trends and excitement around the November 19th launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, we are reiterating our Fiscal 2027 Net Bookings outlook of $8.0 to $8.2 billion.” During a call with analysts, Zelnick said GTA 6 had an “exceptional start to pre-orders,” which kicked off on June 25. However, he did not disclose specific sales numbers. TTWO stock gained as much as 1% in pre-market trade and was among the top trending tickers on Stocktwits at the time of writing. Take-Two reported first-quarter (Q1) revenue of $1.53 billion, ahead of analysts' expectations of $1.36 billion. The company posted a loss of $0.18 per share, compared with Wall Street's expectation for a loss of $0.21 per share, according to Koyfin. However, total net bookings declined 3% year over year to $1.39 billion, compared with $1.42 billion during the same quarter last year. The company's largest contributors to net bookings during the quarter were NBA 2K, the Grand Theft Auto franchise, Toon Blast, Match Factory!, Empires & Puzzles, the Red Dead Redemption series, Words With Friends, Color Block Jam, WWE 2K, Zynga Poker, and Toy Blast. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TTWO stock rose to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ territory over the past day, while chatter stayed at ‘high’ levels. Investor attention remained on Grand Theft Auto VI, which is scheduled for release on November 19 after being delayed from its original fall 2025 launch. The game marks the first mainline Grand Theft Auto release since Grand Theft Auto V debuted in 2013. “I can say that the level of pre-orders is unprecedented and astonishing, and we’re very grateful for that,” Zelnick said during the earnings call. “But they are so unprecedented that we just don’t know how it’ll translate into sales, which is a question I answered earlier. We genuinely don’t, and we just don’t believe in claiming victory before it occurs.” Over the past decade, Grand Theft Auto V has sold more than 215 million copies worldwide, making it the second best-selling video game of all time behind Minecraft. One user said the game could create significant momentum for Take-Two shares in Q4, while another pointed to the company's history of conservative guidance and potential for stronger results following major releases. TTWO stock has fallen nearly 10% this year and gained around 2% in the last 12 months. Airbnb reported earnings per share (EPS) of $1.37 on revenue of $3.61 billion, beating Wall Street estimates of an EPS of $1.22 on revenue of $3.58 billion, according to Fiscal.ai data. Airbnb shares were up more than 8% in Friday’s pre-market trade. According to TheFly, Citizens raised its price target on Airbnb to $190 from $170, while keeping an ‘Outperform’ rating, saying that the company's strong quarter was supported by accelerating bookings growth, resilient travel demand and an expanding set of growth drivers. The firm highlighted hotels, payments, AI-powered products and pricing tools as initiatives that could drive further upside to estimates in the coming quarters. Wells Fargo also lifted its price target to $186 from $181 while maintaining an ‘Overweight’ rating, saying Airbnb's quarterly beat, guidance for accelerating growth and expanding margins mark a “positive inflection” in the company's story. Wedbush upgraded Airbnb to ‘Outperform’ from ‘Neutral’ and raised its price target to $200 from $152, saying the company's early traction from new product initiatives strengthens its long-term growth outlook. The firm said core platform enhancements, including Reserve Now, Pay Later (RNPL) and the rollout of a single-fee pricing model, are supporting the business, while Airbnb's expansion into hotels presents a significant opportunity to capture a larger share of the global travel market. Canaccord also increased its price target to $200 from $180 with a ‘Buy’ rating, citing accelerating growth in nights and experiences booked across both expansion markets and core geographies such as the U.S., France, the U.K. and Australia. UBS raised its price target to $172 from $163 while keeping a ‘Neutral’ rating, saying faster product innovation is helping drive demand growth, operating leverage and improved efficiency. title: West Edmeston Tree No More: Its Journey To NYC Is Underway - CNY News
content: Like many, I have driven past this tree off State Route 8 in West Edmeston for years, it's almost like a local landmark or one of those "oh I know where I am" markers. Now all that's left of the 76-foot Norway Spruce are the memories and lots of pictures. This process didn't happen overnight, it's a month's long endeavor with various local state and Rockefeller Center groups coming together to bring a showstopping spectacle to New York City for millions to see. READ MORE: The 2026 Rockefeller Tree Has Been Chosen, From Central New York Shortly before 7am November 5th, cranes were in place ready to lift this year's Rockefeller Tree from the ground and onto a flatbed. Family and friends gathered at the sight surrounded by plenty of media buzz as well. Current owners of the property at 6526 New York 8 we're excited to see the joy that one tree can bring to millions of people around the world. Rebecca Decker told us once she found out the tree's history and the fact this Christmas 2026 marked the 10th anniversary of the death of the person who planted it, she didn't think twice about donating it. Decker remembered the moment someone from the Rockefeller Center first came to her door and asked about the tree. Erik Pauzé, head gardener and head tree scout for Rockefeller Center was that person. Pauzé remembered when he first saw the tree and made sure to write the address down for a potential future tree. As the hour passed by, crews began their finishing touches before the chainsaw came out. There was some laughter and at one point some were spectacle that the tree was going to come down. The chainsaw operator had a difficult time getting the saw to start. But eventually the engine came to life and the cutting started. Within five minutes, the tree was hoisted above its stump. Cheers from the crowd could be heard and I'm sure some happy tears as well. Crews took a once vertical standing tree and carefully laid it horizontal onto the flatbed. From cut to truck, the process took well over an hour. The only thing left was a plot of dirt once shadowed by the Norway Spruce. By Saturday, the once West Edmeston tree will be in New York City for the annual meet the tree day celebration. We were told that 50 thousand lights are set to light up this tree and the official tree lighting ceremony takes place December 2nd at 7pm. title: Social landlords report tenant satisfaction rise in latest TSM results - HQN
content:
English social landlords have reported an increase in the average level of tenant satisfaction, the Regulator of Social Housing (RSH) has revealed. The latest Tenant Satisfaction Measures (TSM) results show an average increase from 72% last year to 74% for 2025/26 for tenants living in low-cost rental accommodation (LCRA). Telephone surveys remain the most widely used collection method and the RSH says overall satisfaction has increased in every collection method, including by telephone where the proportion of tenants reporting they are satisfied overall has increased from 71% to 73%. The new data also shows that landlords have reported improvements in their repairs and maintenance services, with 83% of non-emergency repairs completed on time in 2025/26, compared to 77% in 2023/24. Average (median) satisfaction with the timeliness of repairs has risen from 67% in 2023/24 to 73% in 2025/26, the largest increase across the tenant perception TSMs. Satisfaction with the maintenance of the home has increased from 71% to 74% over the same period. The vast majority of homes owned by large landlords, as at 31 March 2026, had required gas (99.7%), fire (98.9%), asbestos (98.7%), water (98.2%) and lift safety checks (98.0%) completed. These have each increased since TSMs began in 2023/24, with asbestos, water and lift safety having the comparatively largest increases. And 86% of over 319,000 stage one complaints made during 2025/26 were responded to within the Housing Ombudsman’s Complaint Handling Code timescales. This has increased from 73% in the first year of collection (2023/24). The TSMs also provide landlords with valuable information as to how services might be further improved. Around one in six (16%) of LCRA tenants surveyed are dissatisfied with the overall service from their landlord. Overall average (landlord median) satisfaction for low-cost homeownership (LCHO) remains lower (50%) than LCRA, showing that landlords have work to do to improve services and satisfaction for shared owners, the RSH says. Kate Dodsworth, RSH Deputy Chief Executive, said: “The TSM results are based on feedback from almost half a million tenants, providing the most comprehensive view of tenant satisfaction across large social landlords in England. “The increased level of tenant satisfaction reported by landlords underlines the value of landlords listening to tenants, understanding the issues that matter most to them and using those insights to improve services. “Tenant feedback is one of the most important tools landlords have for assessing performance.
